screens.title: Staff
screens.summary: Who works here, their PINs, phones and pay. The screen has four tabs (People, The schedule, The hours, Shop's clock); this entry covers the top of the screen and the People tab.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Staff. Also: Payroll → “Staff, the schedule and the hours →”; links to /staff#people, /staff#schedule, /staff#attendance, /staff#shop-clock open that tab; /staff#add-person opens the Add people form (Getting set up uses it).

who.owner: everything on the screen: add people, their details, PINs, pay, phones, last days; the schedule; correct hours; make and remove clock screens Not: —
who.general_manager: the same as the owner Not: —
who.branch_manager: add people, change their details, set PINs, link phones, set last days, make the schedule, correct and add hours; see the clock screens Not: see or set pay (no pay badges, no Pay tab, no labour cost in the schedule check); make or remove a clock screen
who.accountant: see everyone and their pay; set pay (Pay tab); see the schedule with its labour cost, and the hours Not: add people, change details, PINs, phones or last days; change the schedule; correct hours; the Shop's clock tab is not shown
who.auditor: read everything on People, The schedule and The hours, pay included Not: change anything; the Shop's clock tab is not shown
who.cashier: nothing here: opening /staff sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.barista: nothing here: opening /staff sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.inventory_counter: nothing here: opening /staff sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.purchasing: nothing here: opening /staff sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen

what_if.case: A new barista starts tomorrow
what_if.do: Add people → fill a row with their name, job, place, tomorrow's date; let them type a PIN or set it later. They show “Starts later” until then.

what_if.case: Someone forgot their PIN
what_if.do: Open their line → New PIN, and let them type a new one twice. It also lifts the pause after too many wrong PINs.

what_if.case: Someone lost their phone
what_if.do: Open their line → Their phone → Unlink… with why. Then link the new phone with Link a new phone. Meanwhile they clock in with their PIN.

what_if.case: Someone leaves at the end of the month
what_if.do: Open their line → Last day, choose the date, write why, Save their last day. Make sure they are clocked out. Their last payroll still includes them.

what_if.case: Someone who left comes back
what_if.do: Open their line → Works here again, write why, They work here again. Then put them on the schedule again.

what_if.case: Two people have the same name
what_if.do: Add a surname or a nickname; the screen refuses two identical names.

tips: Let each person type their own PIN; do not choose it for them.
The CSV opens in Excel or Google Sheets; amounts are plain numbers you can add up.
Add several people at once with Another row; empty rows are skipped.

screens.title: Staff → The schedule
screens.summary: Who works when at a place, a week (Saturday to Friday) at a time, typed as 08:00-16:00; and a check of the week against how busy each part of the day usually is, with what the hours cost.
screens.get_there: Staff → The schedule tab (or /staff#schedule).

who.owner: type and save the week, copy last week, see the check with labour cost Not: —
who.general_manager: type and save the week, copy last week, see the check with labour cost Not: —
who.branch_manager: type and save the week, copy last week, see the check of people needed Not: see the labour cost row and line (no payroll.view)
who.accountant: see the week (read-only) and the check with labour cost Not: change the hours
who.auditor: see the week (read-only) and the check with labour cost Not: change the hours

what_if.case: Make next week's schedule
what_if.do: Press The week after, then The same hours as the week before, change what differs, and Save the week. Check the staffing check before saving.

what_if.case: A shift goes past midnight
what_if.do: Type it as 18:00-02:00; it ends the next morning and counts in the Evening.

what_if.case: Someone swaps a day
what_if.do: Clear their box on that day, type the hours in the other person's box, Save the week.

what_if.case: Saved the wrong week
what_if.do: Press Undo within 10 seconds; later, correct the boxes and save again.

tips: Nothing is saved until Save the week; switching tabs keeps what you typed.
The check updates as you type, so try changes before saving.
Lateness only counts after the café's grace (5 minutes unless changed on Settings → Rules).

screens.title: Staff → The hours
screens.summary: Each day's hours for the week shown: scheduled against clocked, late, left early, absent, overtime; and every record of hours, which a manager corrects, cancels or adds with a reason.
screens.get_there: Staff → The hours tab (or /staff#attendance). The week is the one chosen on The schedule (?week=).

who.owner: see, correct, cancel and add hours Not: change hours in a month whose payroll is approved
who.general_manager: see, correct, cancel and add hours Not: change hours in a month whose payroll is approved
who.branch_manager: see, correct, cancel and add hours Not: change hours in a month whose payroll is approved
who.accountant: see the hours Not: correct, cancel or add
who.auditor: see the hours Not: correct, cancel or add

what_if.case: Someone forgot to clock out
what_if.do: Find their open record (Still in, perhaps “Clocked in a long time”) → Correct… → type the real Out time and why → Save the correction.

what_if.case: The till was down and nobody could clock in
what_if.do: + Add hours nobody clocked… for each person, with In, Out and why.

what_if.case: Someone clocked in the wrong person
what_if.do: Cancel… that record with why, then add the right person's hours.

what_if.case: Late or absent: do they lose pay?
what_if.do: Not automatically. Deduct it on the payroll line (Adjust…) with a note if the café decides so.

tips: Change the week with the arrows on The schedule tab; this tab follows it.
Every correction keeps who made it and why; nothing is deleted.

screens.title: Staff → Shop's clock
screens.summary: The shop's clock screens: devices at the shop (the till, or a tablet by the door) that show a code staff scan with their own phones to clock in and out. The owner makes a device a clock screen from that device.
screens.get_there: Staff → Shop's clock tab (or /staff#shop-clock), on the device that should show the code.

who.owner: make this device a clock screen, take any clock screen out of use Not: —
who.general_manager: make this device a clock screen, take any clock screen out of use Not: —
who.branch_manager: see the clock screens and open the code on this device if it is one Not: make or remove a clock screen
who.accountant: nothing: the tab is not shown Not: see the tab
who.auditor: nothing: the tab is not shown Not: see the tab

what_if.case: The tablet by the door broke
what_if.do: Take out of use… its row with why. On the new tablet, sign in, open Staff → Shop's clock, Make this device a clock screen too.

what_if.case: A tablet anyone can touch is signed in as the owner
what_if.do: Open Show the code on the whole screen and press Sign out, keep the code. The code keeps showing.

tips: Making a clock screen must be done on that very device.
The code is new every 30 seconds, so a photo of it does not work from home.

screens.title: Settings → People and roles
screens.summary: The logins of the people who use the app (members): add someone by email and roles, change their roles and where they work, deactivate or reactivate them. Different from Staff, which lists who works and clocks in.
screens.get_there: Menu → Settings → People and roles (or /settings#people).

who.owner: everything, including giving or taking the owner and general manager roles Not: deactivate themselves; leave the café without an active owner
who.general_manager: add people, change roles and places, deactivate Not: give or take the owner or general manager roles, or change the access of an owner or general manager
who.others: nothing: Settings needs settings.manage Not: open Settings

what_if.case: A new cashier needs to sign in
what_if.do: Add a person with their email and Cashier. Ask them to open the app → First time here? Create your login, with that email, and confirm the email. Then add them on Staff and choose their login.

what_if.case: Someone leaves
what_if.do: Deactivate them here, and set their Last day on Staff.

what_if.case: A branch manager moves branch
what_if.do: Change Where {name} works to the new place.

tips: Members (who signs in) and Staff (who works and clocks in) are two lists; a person can be on both, linked by “Their login” on Staff.

screens.title: Payroll
screens.summary: Each month's pay, drafted from the pay set on Staff and the hours worked; who shares the tips; and advances on pay, which the next payroll takes back.
screens.get_there: Menu → Spending → Payroll. Also: Staff → People → “Payroll and advances →”.

who.owner: draft, adjust, approve, pay, reopen, cancel payments; give and cancel advances; choose who shares the tips Not: —
who.general_manager: draft, adjust, approve, pay, reopen, cancel payments; give and cancel advances; choose who shares the tips Not: —
who.accountant: draft, adjust, approve, pay, reopen, cancel payments; give and cancel advances; choose who shares the tips Not: —
who.auditor: see every payroll, the tips and the advances Not: change anything
who.branch_manager: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.cashier: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.barista: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.inventory_counter: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.purchasing: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen

what_if.case: Someone needs money before payday
what_if.do: + Give an advance… → choose them, the amount, where the money comes from and why → Give the advance. The next payroll takes it back.

what_if.case: An advance was entered twice
what_if.do: Cancel… the extra one with why (only before a payroll took any of it back).

what_if.case: The drawer does not hold enough
what_if.do: Choose The safe or The bank, or move cash into the till first.

what_if.case: A new waiter should share tips
what_if.do: Tick them in Who shares the tips and Save. It counts from today.

tips: Draft last month early in the new month; drafting again after corrections keeps the additions and deductions.

screens.title: Payroll {no}: {month}
screens.summary: One month's payroll: each person's pay from their hours, what was added and deducted with why, advances taken back, what is to be paid and what has been. A draft is adjusted and approved once the month is over; an approved one is paid or reopened.
screens.get_there: Payroll → the number or month of a payroll; also straight after Draft the payroll.

who.owner: draft, adjust, approve, pay, reopen, cancel payments; give and cancel advances; choose who shares the tips Not: —
who.general_manager: draft, adjust, approve, pay, reopen, cancel payments; give and cancel advances; choose who shares the tips Not: —
who.accountant: draft, adjust, approve, pay, reopen, cancel payments; give and cancel advances; choose who shares the tips Not: —
who.auditor: see every payroll, the tips and the advances Not: change anything
who.branch_manager: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.cashier: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.barista: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.inventory_counter: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen
who.purchasing: nothing: opening /payroll sends them to their own start screen Not: open the screen

what_if.case: Someone was late a lot and the café deducts it
what_if.do: Adjust… their line → Deducted with a note (e.g. late 6 times) → Save. Lateness is never deducted by itself.

what_if.case: An Eid bonus
what_if.do: Adjust… → Added with “Eid bonus” → Save.

what_if.case: Approved with a mistake
what_if.do: If nothing is paid: Reopen… with why, fix (pay on Staff, hours, or the line), Draft it again, Approve. If paid: cancel the payments first.

what_if.case: Paid the wrong person
what_if.do: Salaries paid → Cancel… with why, then Pay… the right line.

what_if.case: Pay part now, the rest later
what_if.do: Pay… on the line with a smaller Amount; the rest stays owed.

tips: Leave “Advance taken back” empty to take back everything owed, as far as the pay goes.
Print or save as PDF gives a copy to keep or sign.

screens.title: Clock in or out (at the till)
screens.summary: The till's clock: each person chooses their name and types their PIN. On a clock screen it shows the shop's code first, for those who clock on their phone.
screens.get_there: On the till (POS), the clock button in the top bar (“Clock in or out”). Once the café has a clock screen, the button shows only on a till that is a clock screen.

who.cashier: open it on the till and clock anyone in or out with that person's PIN Not: clock someone without their PIN
who.barista: open it on the till and clock anyone in or out with that person's PIN Not: clock someone without their PIN
who.branch_manager: open it on the till and clock anyone in or out with that person's PIN Not: clock someone without their PIN
who.general_manager: open it on the till and clock anyone in or out with that person's PIN Not: clock someone without their PIN
who.owner: open it on the till and clock anyone in or out with that person's PIN Not: clock someone without their PIN

what_if.case: A person's name is greyed
what_if.do: They have no PIN (a manager sets one on Staff), or they clock with their phone.

tips: Each person types their own PIN; the till's cashier does not need to know it.

screens.title: (the person's name) — the phone's clock
screens.summary: Clocking in or out on your own phone. Scanning the shop's code opens this with the code in it: one press and it is done. The phone is known by a key it keeps since a manager linked it; nobody types a PIN.
screens.get_there: Scan the code on the shop's clock screen with the phone's camera and open the link. Or open /clock and type the 6 digits.

who.anyone with a linked phone: clock themselves in and out, signed in or not Not: clock anyone else; clock from away from the shop (the code changes every 30 seconds)

what_if.case: The scan opens but the code has changed
what_if.do: Type the 6 digits the screen shows now, and press the button.

what_if.case: No phone, or the battery is dead
what_if.do: Clock in at the clock screen (Clock in or out on the till) with your name and PIN — unless your phone is linked: then a manager adds the hours.

what_if.case: Forgot to clock out yesterday
what_if.do: Ask a manager to correct the hours on Staff; then clock in.

tips: Add the page to the phone's home screen to open it quickly.
The code works only at the shop: it changes every 30 seconds.

screens.title: Link this phone
screens.summary: Opened on a person's own phone from the square a manager shows on Staff. One press makes this phone theirs, to clock in and out without a PIN.
screens.get_there: Scan the square on Staff → their line → Their phone, or open the link sent to them. A link works once and for ten minutes.

who.the person whose phone it is: link their own phone, signed in or not Not: —

what_if.case: The link opened in a chat app's browser
what_if.do: Open it in the phone's own browser (Chrome or Safari) and press Link this phone there: the key stays in that browser.

tips: Clearing the browser's data unlinks the phone in practice: ask for a new link.

screens.title: The shop's code (whole screen)
screens.summary: The shop's code in large, for a tablet by the door: a square to scan and its 6 digits, new every 30 seconds.
screens.get_there: Staff → Shop's clock → Show the code on the whole screen (on the clock screen device).

who.any device made a clock screen: show the code, signed in or not Not: —

what_if.case: The till's own clock is wrong
what_if.do: Nothing: the code comes from the server's clock.

tips: Leave the tablet on this page, plugged in, by the door.

screens.title: My account
screens.summary: Everyone's own page: who they are and what they may do, where they start, two-step sign-in, their approval PIN, warnings on this phone, their password, and Sign out.
screens.get_there: Your name at the top right, or Menu → You → My account. People with no screen of their own land here.

who.every signed-in person: see their details, choose a first screen (if they have more than one screen), turn two-step sign-in on or off, change their password, sign out Not: change their own roles
who.owner: also turn on warnings on this phone (when the owner has turned them on for the café) Not: —
who.general_manager: also turn on warnings on this phone (when the owner has turned them on for the café) Not: —
who.branch_manager: also turn on warnings on this phone (when the owner has turned them on for the café) Not: —
who.accountant: also turn on warnings on this phone (when the owner has turned them on for the café) Not: —
who.auditor: also turn on warnings on this phone (when the owner has turned them on for the café) Not: —

what_if.case: Someone may know my password
what_if.do: Change password here, and turn on two-step sign-in.

what_if.case: I lost the phone with the authenticator app
what_if.do: This screen cannot help without the code: ask whoever runs the system to remove the second step, then turn it on again with the new phone.

what_if.case: I want the app in Kurdish
what_if.do: Choose کوردی in the Language list at the top.

tips: The owner should turn on two-step sign-in.
The approval PIN is yours; the clock-in PIN is set on Staff.

screens.title: Test your devices
screens.summary: Before opening, try each of the till's devices in turn — the internet, the receipt printer and its drawer, the label printer, the scanner, the scale's labels, the phone warnings. Nothing here is a sale or goes in the books.
screens.get_there: Menu → You → Test your devices. Also Find anything: “Test your devices”.

what_if.case: The receipt prints too small or cut
what_if.do: In the print dialog set the paper to 80 mm and margins to none, then print the test again.

tips: The ticks are not kept: the screen starts fresh each time.
Nothing printed here is a sale or touches stock or money.

screens.title: Welcome back
screens.summary: The sign-in page: sign in with the email the café invited; or create your login the first time; or ask for a password reset link.
screens.get_there: Any page while signed out; Sign out.

who.anyone: sign in, create a login with an invited email, ask for a reset link Not: get into the café without being invited (Settings → People and roles)

what_if.case: Signed in but sees “Your login is not linked to the business yet”
what_if.do: The email used is not the invited one. Ask the owner to add it on Settings → People and roles, then sign out and in.

tips: Use exactly the email the owner typed when inviting you.

screens.title: One more step
screens.summary: The second step of signing in, for people who turned on two-step sign-in: the six digits from the authenticator app.
screens.get_there: Automatically after the password, or when opening any page with only the password given.

who.anyone with two-step sign-in on: finish signing in Not: open any page before this step

what_if.case: The phone with the app is lost
what_if.do: See open questions: the screen offers no recovery.

tips: The code changes every 30 seconds; type the one showing now.

screens.title: Reports
screens.summary: The reports hub: one long page that reads the café's figures for the dates (and the place) you choose. This entry covers the top of the page: the dates and place, printing, the period at a glance, what the period says, where the money went, the jump links and the links to the other reports. The report sections below it have their own entries (Profit, Sales, Buying and stock, People, Checks).
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports (for some people it sits under More). It is the first screen for the accountant and the auditor. Also: the Dashboard's figures open it; Sales analysis and the week and month pages link back to it.

who.owner: See every part of the page, every report link (the Watch list too), and post the journals the old app never wrote (under Do the books tie?).
who.general_manager: See every part of the page and every report link; the Watch list link only when the owner allows it. Not: Post the journals the old app never wrote (the page says "Only the owner can post them.").
who.branch_manager: See every part of the page, the profit, the exceptions, the staff hours and the customers. Someone who works at one place reads that place only. Not: See what staff cost (the Salaries (6100) table needs payroll.view); see the Watch list.
who.accountant: See every part of the page, the staff hours with what staff cost, the profit, the exceptions and the customers. Not: See the Watch list; post the old app's journals.
who.auditor: The same as the accountant: read every part. Not: Change anything; see the Watch list.
who.purchasing: Open the page and read sales, buying, stock, losses and the checks. Not: See the Profit part, the period's figures at a glance, where each 1,000 IQD went, Exceptions, Staff, Customers and loyalty, or the links to Cash ahead and Balance sheet and cash flow.
who.cashier: Not: Open Reports: they are sent to their own first screen (the till).
who.barista: Not: Open Reports: they are sent to Production.
who.inventory_counter: Not: Open Reports: they are sent to the count.

what_if.case: The figures look wrong
what_if.do: Check the first sentence of What the period says: if the books do not tie, open Do the books tie? and fix the differences first.

what_if.case: You want last month's report on paper
what_if.do: Press Last month, open the parts you want, then Print or save as PDF.

what_if.case: You want one branch only
what_if.do: Choose it in Place and press Show. Remember the four parts named in the note stay the whole café's.

what_if.case: A report you use a lot is at the end of the row
what_if.do: Just keep using it: from its third opening it moves ahead of those you open less.

tips: Every tile, sentence and many numbers are links: tap a number to see what is behind it.
The days compared are always as many as you chose, just before them: choose a whole month to compare with the month before only when both have the same number of days.
The CSV files open in Excel or Google Sheets.

screens.title: Reports — Profit
screens.summary: The profit and loss for the dates, from the published journals, and, when the whole café is read and it has more than one place, each place's profit and loss side by side.
screens.get_there: Reports → the Profit links in the jump links, or the tiles at the top.

who.owner: See both tables and download them.
who.general_manager: See both tables and download them.
who.branch_manager: See both tables and download them.
who.accountant: See both tables and download them.
who.auditor: See both tables and download them.
who.purchasing: Not: See this part (it needs profit.view).

what_if.case: Net revenue here and the till's sales differ
what_if.do: Net revenue is sales less discounts and refunds, with a refund on the day it was made. Check Do the books tie? (the Sales check) and the Sales by Channel note.

what_if.case: An expense is missing
what_if.do: It may be a draft journal or recorded with another date: look on the Journal register or Expenses.

what_if.case: Gross profit is much lower than the sales margin
what_if.do: Gross profit also takes off waste, count differences, price differences on deliveries and platform fees: look at Losses and the cost-of-sales lines.

tips: Gross profit after waste & fees is not the same as the Sales margin in Sales by Channel: the margin is before waste, counts and fees.

screens.title: Reports — Sales
screens.summary: What was sold in the dates: by part of the menu, by channel, the margin of every product today, sizes and add-ons, the ways customers paid, dollars taken and exchanged, and customers with their points.
screens.get_there: Reports → Sales in the jump links.

who.owner: See every section here.
who.general_manager: See every section here.
who.branch_manager: See every section here.
who.purchasing: Not: See Customers and loyalty (needs customer.view).

what_if.case: A product's margin is red
what_if.do: Its cost is above its price on that channel: change the price or the recipe on Products & Recipes.

what_if.case: Cost shows "unknown"
what_if.do: The product has no recipe, or an ingredient has no cost yet: give it a recipe, or record a delivery or opening stock for the item.

what_if.case: A dollar exchange shows a red difference
what_if.do: Less was received than the dollars were taken at; it goes to 6950. Check the rate used at the till.

tips: Sales by Channel's Net sales equals the P&L's Net revenue for the same dates; if not, look at Do the books tie?.

screens.title: Reports — Buying and stock
screens.summary: What was ordered, delivered, returned and credited in the dates; what is owed to suppliers today and how late; the batches made and what became of them; and everything lost or given away.
screens.get_there: Reports → Buying and stock in the jump links.

who.owner: See every section here.
who.general_manager: See every section here.
who.branch_manager: See every section here.

what_if.case: A loss waits for a manager
what_if.do: Approve or reverse it on Approvals (or Inventory); until then it counts in the total.

what_if.case: A supplier's price went up
what_if.do: Open Price watch to see what it does to each product's margin and the price that keeps it.

what_if.case: Much is more than 30 days late
what_if.do: Pay those first on Vendors.

tips: Reversed losses are listed (struck through) but left out of every total.

screens.title: Reports — People (Staff)
screens.summary: The hours the staff worked in the dates, lateness, leaving early and absence, and, for those who see pay, what salaries cost against the sales.
screens.get_there: Reports → People → Staff in the jump links.

who.owner: See the hours and the Salaries (6100) table.
who.general_manager: See the hours and the Salaries (6100) table.
who.accountant: See the hours and the Salaries (6100) table.
who.auditor: See the hours and the Salaries (6100) table.
who.branch_manager: See the hours. Not: See the Salaries (6100) table (needs payroll.view).

what_if.case: Someone shows absent but worked
what_if.do: Their clock-in is missing: correct their attendance on Staff.

tips: Staffed when busy? (in the report links) sets orders an hour against who was on the clock.

screens.title: Reports — Checks
screens.summary: Whether the books tie (every record against its account), the stock the old app never journaled, sales that went out with no cost, and the exceptions: voids, refunds, discounts, cancelled bills, items taken off bills and wrong PINs, by person.
screens.get_there: Reports → Checks in the jump links, or the first sentence of What the period says.

who.owner: See everything and post the old app's journals.
who.general_manager: See everything. Not: Post the old app's journals.
who.branch_manager: See everything. Not: Post the old app's journals.
who.accountant: See everything. Not: Post the old app's journals.
who.auditor: See everything. Not: Post the old app's journals.
who.purchasing: See Do the books tie? and Uncosted Sales. Not: See Exceptions (needs audit.view); post anything.

what_if.case: Inventory (1200) does not tie and the old app's records are listed
what_if.do: Owner: check the records are real, type why, press Post these journal(s). Then look at the check again.

what_if.case: The drawer check does not tie
what_if.do: Open its Subledger link (Drawer sessions): a session not yet counted or closed is the usual cause.

what_if.case: A cashier has many voids for review
what_if.do: Read each void's reason and time in the list; talk to them; from now on a second person can approve voids at the till.

tips: Do the books tie? reads as at the end of To; Payable Ageing reads today.

screens.title: Sales analysis
screens.summary: The sales of the dates seen one way and, if you like, a second (by hour, day, product, person, payment…), narrowed to a channel, branch, category or person, with what each made, cost and kept after refunds.
screens.get_there: Reports → Sales analysis: by hour, day, product, person, payment… →. Also from the week and month pages, and from sentences on Reports.

who.owner: Use every choice. Someone who works at one place sees that place's sales only.
who.general_manager: Use every choice. Someone who works at one place sees that place's sales only.
who.branch_manager: Use every choice. Someone who works at one place sees that place's sales only.
who.accountant: Use every choice. Someone who works at one place sees that place's sales only.
who.auditor: Use every choice. Someone who works at one place sees that place's sales only.
who.purchasing: Use every choice. Someone who works at one place sees that place's sales only.
who.cashier: Not: Open it (sent to their own first screen).
who.barista: Not: Open it (sent to their own first screen).
who.inventory_counter: Not: Open it (sent to their own first screen).

what_if.case: Which hours are busiest?

screens.title: Where people get stuck
screens.summary: For the owner: each time the database refuses something on a screen, or someone opens a screen's help, it is noted. This report lists the screens that stop people most over the last 7, 30 or 90 days: how often refused, how often its help was opened, how many people and which roles, and what was said most. Practice is counted apart. Make the top screens plainer, or show people how, before adding more help.

what_if.case: A red alert is a known, harmless thing
what_if.do: Press Answer, write why it is fine, Save the answer. It moves to Answered or snoozed and stays there until the condition clears.

what_if.case: An alert will be dealt with next week
what_if.do: Press Snooze, pick the day, write why it can wait, Snooze it. If it is still true that day it comes back; if it turns from orange to red sooner, it comes back at once.

what_if.case: The exceptions alert names me
what_if.do: You cannot answer it: another manager or the owner reviews it on Reports → Exceptions.

what_if.case: An alert disappeared by itself
what_if.do: Its condition cleared (e.g. the drawer was counted, the bill paid). Nothing else to do.

what_if.case: Thresholds feel too strict or too loose
what_if.do: The owner or general manager changes them on Settings → Alerts (e.g. margin target, hours a session may stay open). An empty box goes back to the default.

what_if.case: No target card
what_if.do: Set the daily sales target on Settings → Rules (the link appears for the owner/GM).

what_if.case: The badge says reconciliation differences
what_if.do: Open it: Reports shows which record and which ledger account disagree.

tips: Every figure is a link: open it to see what is behind it.
Red brings Needs you to the top: if the page starts with alerts, something cannot wait.
Yesterday's brief keeps facts, calculations and what to do apart: a figure is never a judgement.
Steps put aside and a hidden Getting set up list are remembered per device only.
The dashboard's net sales and gross profit are the books' own, the same as the Profit & Loss for today.
